paragraphs.source_en: Miss Tortoiseshell is dead, and Blacky and I do not get on; so I feel somewhat lonely. Fortunately, I have found friends among human beings, and therefore do not feel especially desolate. Not long ago, someone wrote to my master asking him to send a photograph of me. Recently, someone even went to the trouble of sending me, by name, Okayama's famous kibi dumplings. As human beings increasingly extend their sympathy toward me, I gradually forget that I am a cat. I seem to feel that I am no longer a cat, but have gradually drawn nearer to humanity. My former notion of rallying the feline race and deciding superiority with the two-legged gentlemen has lately vanished like smoke. More than that, I have evolved so far that at times I even consider myself one member of the human world, which makes the future seem promising. It is not that I despise my own kind; it is simply natural tendency, and the force of circumstance, to seek peace for oneself where one's nature inclines. If this is judged as a change of heart, fickleness, or betrayal, I should be much wronged. Those who juggle such words and casually revile others are mostly inflexible fellows with a poverty-stricken turn of mind. Having shed my feline habits, it is only natural that I should no longer busy myself solely with Miss Tortoiseshell or great Blacky, but should wish to judge their thoughts, words, and deeds with the same dignity as a human being. Unfortunately, my master still regards me, endowed though I am with such discernment, as nothing more than an ordinary fur-covered cat. Without so much as a word to me, he brazenly ate up every one of the kibi dumplings that had been sent for me. Nor does it appear that he intends to take a decent photograph of me and send it off. If this is called grumbling, then grumbling it certainly is; but my master is my master and I am myself, and since our views naturally differ, there is nothing to be done. Because I persist in considering myself already human, the conduct of other cats with whom I no longer associate is, after all, rather difficult to set down in writing. I shall therefore discharge my duty by speaking only of such gentlemen as Meitei and Kangetsu, and beg the reader's indulgence.

paragraphs.source_zh: 三毛姑娘死了，和老黑又合不来，我多少有些寂寥之感，所幸在人类中有了知己，也就不感到怎样沉寂了。前不久，有人写信给主人，求他把我的照片寄去。最近，还有人特地把冈山的名产“吉备糯米团子”寄来指名给我。随着人类对我寄予同情，我逐渐忘却自己是只猫儿。我似乎觉得自己不再是猫儿，已逐渐向人类靠拢了。我原先想要纠合猫族去和两只脚的先生们决一雌雄的想法，最近已烟消雾散。岂止如此，我已经进化到有时甚至认为自己是人间的一员，感到前途有望。我倒不是瞧不起同族，只是性之所近，求取一身安宁，势所使然。如果认为这是变心、轻浮、背叛，可就错怪我了。像这种咬文嚼字，随便谩骂别人的人，大多是不懂得通融、活该受穷的家伙。我蜕却了猫的习性以后，当然不该再把三毛姑娘或大老黑的事放在心上，我要以和人类同样的气度来评骘他们的思想言行，恐怕这也是很自然的吧。遗憾的是，主人把具有这般见识的我仍然看作一只普普通通披毛带皮的猫儿。他连一声招呼都不打，就大模大样地把寄给我的吉备糯米团子吃个精光。照片看来也不想给我拍好寄去。这要说是牢骚的确是牢骚，不过主人是主人，我是我，彼此见解自然各异，这也是无可奈何的事。因为我始终以为自己已经是个人了，所以对不再交往的其他猫儿的行为，也就有点难于形之笔墨啦。还是讲讲迷亭、寒月几位先生的事儿聊以塞责，敬请读者海涵吧。
